# Architecture and data flow

Native execution:

```text
Python authoring / checked XML or dictionary
    -> fully populated Scene
    -> transactional parameter edits and validation
    -> frozen .cys + asset bundle
    -> native parser -> material graph + BVH + light distributions
    -> camera sample -> spectral path / volume path / photon gather
    -> XYZ accumulation + optional dual/Stokes accumulation
    -> raw float32 film + display conversion + receipts
```

The C++ renderer does not import or invoke Python during transport. The Python API authors, validates, serializes, launches, and inspects it. Changing an XML parameter is not equivalent to changing an arbitrary native plugin class. Independent custom geometry/material authoring factories compile to supported native representations.

The core native files are `math.hpp`, `spectrum.hpp`, `geometry.hpp`, `material.hpp`, `polarization.hpp`, `volume.hpp`, `scene.hpp`, `integrator.hpp`, and `photonmap.hpp`. `texture.hpp` owns PFM texture sampling; `shader.hpp` loads the generated material kernel ABI; `film.hpp` holds persistent sample accumulators and filters; `exr.hpp` is the independent OpenEXR writer. `src/main.cpp` performs indexed, per-pixel OpenMP accumulation. Each pixel receives the same sample sequence regardless of thread scheduling.

`python/cybrlight/workflow.py` owns the checked scene subset and serialized model; `mesh_io.py` owns OBJ/PLY import; `volume_io.py` owns VOL container conversion. `jit.py` is an independent expression DAG and C++ code generator. Native shaders export `cybr_shader(nm,u,v,parameters,value,gradient)` and return a bounded reflectance and its three parameter derivatives. The native dual-number path accumulates those derivatives through multiplications and indirect paths.

`portable_kernel.py` is another renderer using a single scalar source for CPU JIT and CUDA compilation. `portable.py` validates its narrower feature boundary, packs scene arrays and a stackless threaded BVH, launches the chosen target, and labels simulator output explicitly. It uses Numba's compiler. It is not generated by the independent expression compiler, and it is not a hardware-verified replacement for the native backend.

`inverse.py` builds a finite-difference image Jacobian by rerendering small perturbations of scene parameters. It solves a damped bounded least-squares step. Its declared loss filter changes only the optimization objective, not the rendered display images. Parameter derivatives here are numerical estimates, including all changes made by the forward renderer; they are not substituted for an automatic, unbiased visibility derivative estimator.

Source-level interfaces are inspectable and modifiable, but not ABI promises. The native `.cys` format is strict about unsupported directives and trailing fields. The XML/dictionary loader supports the names returned by `cybrlight plugins`, subject to the explicit parameter restrictions in the implementation. An unsupported plugin raises an error; there is no external-renderer fallback.
